articles.title: ASAM: Adaptive cortical surface representation via dynamic local aggregation and hybrid Attention-Mamba global modeling.
articles.abstract: Accurately modeling cortical surface geometry from structural MRI is essential for advancing neuroimaging analysis and biomarker discovery. Recent advances in Transformer and Mamba architectures have shown promise in brain surface modeling by effectively capturing complex feature dependencies. However, they typically rely on fixed or absent neighborhood structures, substantially limiting their ability to represent localized cortical variations. Transformers also incur high computational costs, whereas Mamba lacks explicit mechanisms for encoding local spatial context on non-Euclidean domains. To address these limitations and leverage the complementary strengths of both architectures, we propose ASAM (Adaptive Surface representation with Attention and Mamba), a hybrid framework integrating Transformer and Mamba mechanisms within a parallel architecture. ASAM introduces two novel modules designed specifically for cortical surfaces: Dynamic Multi-Hop Selection (DMHS), which adaptively determines optimal receptive fields for each cortical patch, and Dynamic Feature Merging (DFM), which constructs context-sensitive adjacency matrices from geodesic distances and learned affinities. Extensive evaluations on public neuroimaging datasets demonstrate that ASAM achieves superior or highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art Transformer- and Mamba-based baselines in CN vs. MCI classification on ADNI and cross-dataset brain age prediction. By dynamically adjusting neighborhood scales, ASAM yields enriched, geometry-aware cortical surface representations, supporting neuroimaging research on risk stratification and developmental brain assessments while motivating further multi-center validation toward clinical translation. Implementation code is publicly available at: https://github.com/sydat2701/ASAM_surface.git.

articles.title: In Vivo Ankle Tendon Quantification Using Ultrashort Echo Time Magnetization Transfer Imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To quantitatively assess in vivo ankle tendons using less magic angle-sensitive 3-dimensional ultrashort echo time magnetization transfer (UTE MT) imaging and to compare its intersubject variability with UTE T2* mapping in healthy volunteers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty healthy volunteer ankles were examined on a 3T MRI system using a standardized clinical protocol with additional 3D UTE MT and 3D multi-echo UTE T2* sequences (acquisition times: 4:16 and 9:52 minutes, respectively). Nine major ankle tendons were semi-automatically segmented to extract quantitative UTE MTR and UTE T2* values for each tendon. Variability for each sequence was assessed using the coefficient of variation (CV), and differences in CV were evaluated primarily with a paired bootstrap of the CV ratio and secondarily with a modified signed log-likelihood ratio (MSLR) test, both with Holm correction. Within-tendon angular dependence was assessed using local tendon fiber angles relative to B0. RESULTS: Absolute quantitative values differed between tendons, with the Achilles tendon demonstrating the lowest T2* values (2.15±0.43 ms) and highest MTR values (0.44±0.08), whereas smaller positional tendons showed higher T2* and lower MTR values. UTE MTR demonstrated lower overall variability compared with UTE T2* values across the 9 assessed tendons (overall CV UTE MTR: 18.0%±4.2% vs. UTE T2*: 33.7%±8.9%, mean±SD, n=9). In the paired bootstrap analysis with Holm correction, UTE MTR showed significantly lower variability than UTE T2* in 6 of 9 tendons, with the largest differences in the extensor digitorum longus, peroneus brevis, and flexor hallucis longus tendons (T2*/MTR CV ratio, 2.74, 2.60, and 2.48; all Holm-adjusted P≤0.015); MSLR results were consistent. Between 0 degree and the magic angle, UTE T2* increased by 79% (95% CI: 64%-95%), whereas UTE MTR decreased by 9% (95% CI: 7%-11%). UTE MTR consistently demonstrated reduced dispersion and narrower value distributions compared with UTE T2*. CONCLUSIONS: In vivo ankle tendon quantification using UTE MT is feasible within clinically acceptable acquisition times and shows significantly lower intersubject variability than UTE T2* mapping in most tendons, with reduced susceptibility to the magic angle effect. UTE MT represents a promising approach for quantitative assessment of tendon structure in vivo.

articles.title: Photon-Counting CT for Postoperative Imaging of Cochlear Implants: Comparison to Flat-Detector CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: After FDA approval in 2021, photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCCT) has demonstrated its feasibility for high-resolution imaging while lowering the radiation dose at the same time. High-resolution visualization of cochlear implant (CI) integrity and positioning is crucial for postoperative management. The aim of this study was to evaluate the performance of PCCT for postoperative imaging after CI implantation in comparison to high-resolution flat-detector CT (FDCT), the current clinical gold standard. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Postoperative PCCT scans after cochlear implantation were retrospectively analyzed from August 2024 to April 2026. Scans were included for analysis if FDCT acquisition had been before PCCT on the same patient in the course of sequential bilateral cochlear implantation. Image quality was assessed in consensus by 2 experienced readers using a scoring system analyzing structural delineation of the inner and middle ear, CI integrity, metal and motion artifacts as well as calculating an overall score. Radiation dose was retrieved from the picture archiving and communication system. RESULTS: Twenty-eight postoperative PCCT scans of patients after CI implantation with a mean time delay of 4.5±5.1 years between FDCT and PCCT scans were evaluated. Image quality of PCCT was noninferior to FDCT for all single imaging features (P<0.001, eg, distinction of single CI electrodes: median [interquartile range] PCCT 3 [3 to 3]; FDCT 3 [3 to 3]; P<0.001) with the exception of the homogeneity of bony structures and the mastoid cell septation (P=0.999). PCCT was superior to FDCT in reducing metal and motion artifacts and increasing the delineation of the stapes (P=0.009 to <0.001; eg, metal artifacts PCCT 3 [2.75 to 3]; FDCT 2 [1 to 2]; P<0.001). Effective radiation dose of PCCT was 0.05±0.01 mSv and 8.8±5.4-times lower than for FDCT with 0.44±0.29 mSv (P<0.001) applying our institutional protocols. CONCLUSIONS: Regarding image quality in postoperative assessment of CI, PCCT is noninferior to or in single features better than FDCT at a significantly lower radiation dose and shorter scan time.

articles.title: Tract Sealing in Percutaneous Liver Biopsy: A Systematic Review of Comparative and Single-Arm Studies.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare bleeding-related adverse events after percutaneous liver biopsy with and without tract sealing, separating clinical outcomes from randomized evidence on a surrogate endpoint. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Five databases were searched (2000 to August 2026) for percutaneous liver biopsy with tract sealing by any agent or energy. Adverse events were graded on the Society of Interventional Radiology scale as mild (grade 1) or moderate to fatal (grades 2 to 5). Comparative data were pooled using random-effects models, with the Peto method for major bleeding. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies reporting 4,560 liver biopsy procedures were included. Two retrospective studies compared sealing with no sealing on clinically defined outcomes. Overall bleeding-related adverse events did not differ (OR 0.52; 95% CI 0.13-2.17; P = .370), whereas major bleeding was less frequent with sealing (Peto OR 0.09; 95% CI 0.02-0.42; P = .002; absolute risk difference 3.3%). Two randomized trials favored sealing on a Doppler surrogate but not on clinically significant bleeding. Major bleeding in single-arm cohorts ranged from 0% to 2.2%. Three studies comparing plugged percutaneous with transjugular biopsy allocated patients with worse coagulation indices to the transjugular arm. CONCLUSION: Tract sealing was associated with fewer major bleeding-related adverse events but not fewer events overall. The evidence supports selective use in patients with identifiable bleeding risk but does not establish benefit in unselected low-risk patients.

articles.title: Vertebral Augmentation for Osteoporotic Compression Fractures: Umbrella Review of Adjacent Vertebral Fracture Incidence and Risk Factors.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether vertebral augmentation (VA) increases adjacent vertebral fracture (AVF) risk compared with conservative treatment and identify potential risk factors. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, EBSCOhost, ScienceDirect, and Scopus were searched for systematic reviews and meta-analyses published between 2014 and 2025 evaluating AVFs following VA for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) [PROSPERO: CRD420251079382]. Methodological quality, evidence overlap, and certainty were assessed using AMSTAR-2, corrected covered area (CCA) and weighted CCA (wCCA), and an adapted GRADE framework, respectively. Narrative synthesis followed SWiM due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Reporting followed PRIOR and PRISMA 2020 guidance. RESULTS: Nine systematic reviews and meta-analyses were included. AMSTAR-2 confidence was low in 5/9 and critically low in 4/9 reviews. All 13 GRADE-assessed outcomes had low or very low certainty. Evidence overlap was 5.88% by CCA and 4.66% by wCCA. One review reported a pooled single-arm AVF incidence of approximately 14%, while other reviews reported incidences of 8%-18%. Comparative findings were heterogeneous, with increased, decreased, or no significant difference in AVF risk following VA versus conservative treatment. Lower bone mineral density, female sex, cement leakage, cement volume, and inadequate anti-osteoporosis treatment were reported as potential risk factors, although associations varied and were not consistently specific to adjacent-level fractures. CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not consistently demonstrate increased AVF risk following VA compared with conservative treatment. Heterogeneity, methodological limitations, and low to very low certainty limit definitive conclusions. Standardized fracture definitions, reporting of procedural factors and osteoporosis treatment, and adequately powered prospective studies are required.

articles.title: Circulating Biomarkers for Interventional Oncology: Current Status and Future Direction.
articles.abstract: Biomarkers reflect underlying physiological or pathological processes and support disease detection, cancer diagnosis, treatment selection and prognosis, monitoring of therapeutic response, and identification of disease recurrence in interventional oncology (IO) care. In recent years, liquid biopsy of circulating biomarkers has emerged as a transformative approach in oncology. Given the growing role of IO in cancer care and the potential for circulating biomarkers to directly impact patient care in Interventional Radiology, this narrative review summarizes circulating biomarker types, current detection technologies and workflows, clinical applications in IO care, and next-generation biomarker modalities and detection instruments for Interventional Radiologists.

articles.title: Clinical applications of photon-counting CT in abdominal oncologic imaging: a primer for developing a clinical practice.
articles.abstract: Photon-counting CT (PCCT) is an emerging imaging modality that offers improved spatial resolution, soft tissue contrast, material decomposition, and dose efficiency over conventional CT with energy-integrating detectors (EID-CT). For patients with abdominal malignancies, who routinely undergo cross-sectional imaging for diagnosis, staging, response assessment, and surveillance, PCCT has the potential to enhance the detection and characterization of contrast-enhanced tumors and improve treatment response assessment. The objectives of this review are to provide a comprehensive overview of the technical principles of PCCT, optimization strategies, advantages in abdominal oncologic imaging, and current clinical applications geared towards clinical radiologists. We also address implementation challenges and discuss future directions for integrating PCCT into routine oncologic care. As PCCT utilization increases, its impact on abdominal cancer diagnosis and management is expected to grow, offering new opportunities for precision medicine and personalized imaging strategies.

articles.title: Bidirectional multi-scale implicit neural representation network for topology-aware lung 4D-CT registration.
articles.abstract: Objective.Precise lung 4D-CT registration is extremely challenging due to large respiratory excursions. To capture such large-magnitude motion, existing deep learning methods typically adopt a unidirectional coarse-to-fine cascade strategy, which is vulnerable to error propagation because uncorrected coarse-level misalignments degrade subsequent finer-scale stages and often lead to spatially inconsistent deformations. While implicit neural representations (INRs) support continuous coordinate-based deformation modeling, traditional instance-specific INRs lack clinical efficiency and struggle to converge on global large deformations because of the absence of multi-scale semantic guidance. This study aims to bridge these gaps by developing a bidirectional multi-scale INR network that jointly handles large deformation modeling and localized structural fidelity.Approach.We propose a bidirectional multi-scale INR network. First, a generalized conditional INR framework is introduced to enable continuous deformation modeling without the need for retraining. Crucially, a bidirectional feature feedback mechanism built upon Swin Transformer injects high-level semantic priors into low-resolution streams, correcting coarse-level biases through top-down interaction. Furthermore, an anatomy-aware structural constraint is incorporated to promote anatomical consistency and local boundary alignment.Main results.Under the within-subject phase-held-out DIR-Lab protocol, the proposed method achieved a mean TRE of 1.28 mm and a folding rate of 0.0090%. A leave-one-case-out evaluation assessed subject-independent generalization, yielding a mean TRE of 1.53 mm and a folding rate of 0.0195%. On the independent POPI dataset, the method achieved a mean TRE of 1.84 mm and a folding rate of 0.0806%, demonstrating competitive cross-center performance. Inference took 0.33 s per case.Significance.The proposed framework effectively combines continuous coordinate modeling with deep learning efficiency, overcoming error propagation inherent in discrete coarse-to-fine strategies and preserving both global deformation consistency and local anatomical precision. Its sub-second inference and performance under leave-one-case-out and independent external testing support its potential for efficient image-guided radiation therapy workflows.

articles.title: When US and MRI disagree: association of pre- high-intensity focused ultrasound imaging discordance with technical, safety, and clinical outcomes in uterine fibroid ablation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the prevalence of pre-procedural US-MRI discordance and its association with Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR)-standardized outcomes in patients undergoing US-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation for symptomatic uterine fibroids. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 308 consecutive patients were included. Discordance was defined as mismatch in fibroid type, location, uterine position, or absolute volume percentage difference > 50%. Patients were stratified into concordant (n = 252) and discordant (n = 56) groups. Outcomes were assessed according to SIR domains: technical success (non-perfused volume ratio on day-1 contrast-enhanced MRI), technical efficacy (through six procedural surrogates as a whole: energy-efficiency factor, overall treatment time, cumulative sonication time, treatment intensity, average sonication power, and oxytocin dose), adverse events (SIR classification), and favorable short-term procedural outcome. RESULTS: Discordance occurred in 18.2% of cases. Categorical agreement was high, with Gwet's AC1 > 0.93, and volume agreement was good, with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.773. Day-1 non-perfused volume ratio and technical-success thresholds were comparable between groups. In unadjusted analysis, the energy-efficiency factor was higher after discordant imaging (p = 0.024) and oxytocin use was shifted toward the 60 IU dose (p = 0.036). After adjustment, neither association remained significant (p = 0.191 and 0.228). Adverse-event profiles and the favorable short-term procedural outcome did not differ significantly. CONCLUSION: In this study, pre-HIFU US-MRI discordance was not associated with clear differences in technical success, technical efficacy, adverse events, or short-term procedural outcomes. Recognition of discordance may still help inform procedural planning and patient counseling within SIR-standardized frameworks.

articles.title: Fat Fraction Mapping in the Presence of Magnetic Field Inhomogeneities With Phase-Cycled bSSFP at 3 T.
articles.abstract: Magnetic field inhomogeneities (ΔB0) can cause fat-water swaps in proton density fat fraction (PDFF) mapping using phase-cycled balanced steady-state free-precession (bSSFP). In this work, a graph-cuts-based smoothness-imposing optimization was developed to estimate ΔB0 from phase-cycled bSSFP data obtained in fat-water compartments. Data were acquired in phantoms spanning PDFF of 0%-100% to quantify robustness to ΔB0 and to determine the effect of RF excitation angle (α) on PDFF estimation. The approach was further tested in healthy volunteer knee data (n = 9) and chronic liver disease patients data (n = 5). Phase-cycled bSSFP-based ΔB0 and PDFF maps were compared with multi-echo gradient-echo (MEGRE) reference maps in phantoms and knees. In liver patients, PDFF maps were compared visually and by retrospective ROI analysis with reference quantitative Dixon (qDixon) PDFF maps. Estimated ΔB0 maps matched the reference, with a root-mean-squared error (RMSE) of 9 ± 2 Hz for a ΔB0 range of ±400 Hz in phantoms and 17 ± 4 Hz for a range of ±150 Hz in knees. PDFF mapping accuracy improved after ΔB0 correction, with mean RMSE reduced from 35% ± 9% to 3.55% ± 0.92% and mean R2 increased from 0.29 ± 0.3 to 0.99 ± 0 (p < 0.0001) across the six phantom experiments (mean ± SD of experiments). PDFF quantification showed significant bias for α = 5°, 40°, and 45° (bias = 2.7%, -2.9%, and -5.8%; p < 0.05), whereas no significant bias was observed for 10° ≤ α ≤ 35° (p > 0.05). Mean PDFF differences versus MEGRE reference were 2.4% ± 3%, -0.1% ± 0.8%, and 0.2% ± 0.3% for muscle, subcutaneous fat, and bone marrow, respectively. In liver patients, whole-liver ROI analysis demonstrated a mean PDFF difference of 3% relative to qDixon. Fat-water swaps were successfully removed in knee and patient liver PDFF maps. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately estimates ΔB0 and mitigates fat-water swaps in phantoms and healthy volunteer knees, while the patient liver study demonstrates the technical feasibility of the proposed framework for phase-cycled bSSFP-based PDFF mapping in vivo.

articles.title: Calibration of 3-T MR Relaxometry for Quantitative Liver Iron Assessment Using Human Liver Explants.
articles.abstract: MR relaxometry has become the preferred noninvasive method for estimating hepatic iron from R2 and R2* relaxation rates. However, the precise quantification of liver iron concentration (LIC) requires calibration, and published equations relating relaxation rates to LIC have limited transferability across scanners and acquisition protocols. This study aimed to establish local 3-T calibration equations relating R2 and R2* relaxation rates to chemically determined LIC using human liver explants and to evaluate their applicability in independent in vivo cohorts. Thirty-six human liver explants underwent MR examination on a 3-T system using multi-echo spin-echo and multi-echo gradient-echo sequences to obtain R2 and R2* relaxation rates. LIC was determined chemically by atomic absorption spectrophotometry. Calibration equations were derived using linear regression and compared with previously published models. The R2*-based calibration was subsequently applied to independent in vivo cohorts examined using the same MR system and comparable acquisition protocols. Both MR methods correlated strongly with chemically determined LIC (R2*: r = 0.95, p < 0.001; R2: r = 0.92, p < 0.001). Compared with published models, the local calibrations demonstrated lower prediction errors and narrower limits of agreement within the studied explant cohort. Application of the R2* equation to in vivo datasets yielded physiologically plausible LIC estimates, with the lowest values observed in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis, intermediate values in healthy controls and the highest values in subjects with elevated serum ferritin concentrations. Explant-derived 3-T calibration equations demonstrated strong association with chemically measured LIC and generated physiologically plausible LIC estimates in vivo. These findings support the feasibility of deriving local MR relaxometry calibrations from human liver explants, while further prospective validation against an independent LIC reference is required before clinical application.

articles.title: A condensed matter inspired framework for the FLASH effect in radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The FLASH radiation treatment utilizes ultra-high dose rates (UHDR) with short exposure times, while exhibiting a unique feature of reduced damage to healthy tissues (sparing effect). FLASH physics remains unknown. PURPOSE: To develop a quantitative bio-physical model of FLASH radiation treatment. METHODS: We explore a two-phase system of cancer inclusions embedded in a healthy host. The important morphological difference between the phases is that the cancer phase is structurally disordered, while the healthy host material is more organized. Correspondingly, the recombination times for radiation generated charge carriers are much shorter in the cancer phase than in the normal tissue host phase. RESULTS: In the host material, the nonequilibrium charge density under UHDR can be high enough to form electron-hole liquid suppressing generation of active radicals; hence, sparing effect. A disordered tumor phase renders channels producing radicals capable of cells destruction. The FLASH thresholds for dose and dose rates are predicted. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed two-phase model provides quantitative description of FLASH radiation treatment.

articles.title: Fully Automated Segmentation of Chronic Total Occlusion Lesions on Coronary CT Angiography Using Deep Learning.
articles.abstract: Reliable quantitative assessment for chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions depends on accurate segmentation of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) images. However, incomplete contrast opacification and complex lesion morphology make precise delineation particularly challenging. We developed an Atrous Attention U-Net (AAU-Net) for CTO segmentation and integrated it into a fully automated workflow comprising heart localization, CTO localization, and lesion segmentation. This retrospective study included 565 CTO lesions from 551 patients who underwent prospectively ECG-gated CCTA at three centers. Standalone segmentation used reference-mask-derived lesion-containing slices and regions of interest, whereas the automated workflow used predicted localization without reference-mask information or manual correction. Under reference-defined localization, AAU-Net achieved a Dice score of 0.8421 and intersection over union of 0.7312 in the internal test set, although performance varied by anatomical location and center. Performance decreased in the fully automated workflow, with Dice scores of 0.6922 in the internal test set, 0.5822 in external test set 1, and 0.6480 in external test set 2, potentially reflecting localization errors and differences between the separately trained segmentation models. In an exploratory locked-model radiomics analysis, features derived from automated segmentations showed numerically lower predictive performance than those derived from manual segmentations. Overall, AAU-Net showed favorable segmentation performance under reference-defined localization, but the fully automated workflow demonstrated lower performance that varied across centers. The radiomics findings demonstrate technical feasibility rather than established clinical utility. Further optimization and larger prospective multicenter validation are required before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Networks for 3D Coronary Artery Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction of coronary artery geometry from computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived segmentations is challenging because of thin vessel walls, tortuous trajectories, and small distal structures. We propose a physics-informed implicit neural network (PIINN) for case-specific reconstruction of paired coronary surfaces from pre-segmented CCTA-derived lumen and outer-wall geometries. For each coronary segment, a single network is optimized independently to represent the luminal and outer vessel-wall surfaces using dual signed distance fields (SDFs). The objective combines supervised SDF regression and boundary anchoring with Eikonal regularization and geometry- and anatomy-informed soft constraints on surface ordering, enclosure consistency, and local wall separation. A three-stage curriculum progressively adjusts the spatial sampling, learning rate, and constraint weights. The framework was evaluated on 15 coronary artery segments. The PIINN (256 × 6) achieved a near-surface RMSE of 0.26 mm and a sign accuracy approaching 90% for the outer SDF. Mesh reconstruction achieved an inner-surface ASSD of 0.166 mm and an HD95 of 0.455 mm, compared with the ASSD values of 0.290 mm for Vanilla INR and 1.057 mm for DeepSDF, with statistically significant improvements across the evaluated cases (p ≤ 0.003). Component-wise ablation further demonstrated distinct contributions from Eikonal regularization, anatomical constraints, region-based sampling, and curriculum optimization. These results support PIINN as a constrained continuous representation for case-specific coronary reconstruction from CCTA-derived segmentations; direct reconstruction from raw CCTA and generalization to unseen patients were not evaluated.

articles.title: Tumor Semantic Modeling with Vascular Morphology Prior Correction Reduces False-Positive Malignant Predictions on Contrast-Enhanced Lung CT.
articles.abstract: To develop an interpretable contrast-enhanced CT-based framework for benign-malignant lung tumor classification by integrating radiology-style semantic representations with global pulmonary vascular morphology features. Two particular difficulties with this task lie in (1) establishing an interpretable model to distinguish tumor data that are difficult to differentiate between benign and malignant in clinical practice, and (2) based on clinical experience, incorporate the vascular characteristics around the tumor into the decision-making process. We propose a vascular knowledge-enhanced classification framework that integrates semantic tumor representations extracted by large multimodal models with peritumoral vascular morphological features. The framework consists of three components: (1) an interpretable feature extractor for tumor representation learning, (2) vascular morphology modeling derived from vessel segmentation, and (3) a feature fusion module combining tumor and vascular information for classification. In a retrospective cohort of 420 patients with pathologically confirmed pulmonary tumors, the proposed method was assessed using patient-level, stratified five-fold cross-validation. Relative to the semantic-only branch, decision-level fusion increased accuracy (71.4% vs. 75.5%), AUC (0.764 vs. 0.816), and specificity (57.3% vs. 77.8%), but decreased sensitivity (81.1% vs. 73.9%). These findings indicate that vascular prior-guided correction primarily enhanced benign-case recognition and suppressed false-positive malignant predictions, at the expense of sensitivity for malignant cases. In single-center validation, pulmonary vascular morphology offered complementary structural evidence for differentiating benign from malignant pulmonary tumors larger than 3 cm. The proposed AND-like decision-level correction rule enhanced specificity by reducing false-positive malignant predictions.

articles.title: Embedding a Consolidated Resource Panel in the PACS Worklist: Implementation and First-Year Adoption.
articles.abstract: Radiologists rely on many resources during a shift, including imaging protocols, policies, call schedules, phone directories, and IT support tools. At our institution, each lives in a separate location outside the picture archiving and communication system (PACS), so reaching any of them meant leaving PACS. We built a static web page that gathers the links and reference material radiologists use most often, styled it to match the PACS interface, and embedded it in the worklist window by repurposing a display panel the PACS vendor provides for messages and alerts. Self-hosted web analytics recorded how it was used. Over the first 12 months, the panel recorded 58,524 visits and 10,253 outbound resource clicks. It was available to approximately 200 attending radiologists, residents, and fellows, roughly 90 of whom work on a typical weekday, and generated a median of 40 outbound clicks per steady-state weekday. Because the analytics identify workstations rather than people, unique-visitor counts exceed headcount and cannot be expressed as a per-person adoption rate. Clicks concentrated in a few everyday tools; paging, the report database, and the call schedule accounted for about two-thirds. These data document sustained use. This implementation and adoption report describes how the platform was built, embedded, and measured, and how other departments can reproduce it. The source code is publicly available.

articles.title: CIRSE 2026 Book of Abstracts.
Achieving Complete Pathologic Necrosis Before Liver Transplantation for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Single-center Analysis of 16.5-Year Trends in Locoregional Therapy in 246 Patients.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether complete pathologic necrosis (CPN) after locoregional therapy is associated with post-transplant outcomes, and whether achieving CPN varies by tumor size, treatment modality, or has changed over time. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing locoregional therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma before liver transplantation at a single center from January 2010 to June 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Recurrence was analyzed by Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence. Lesion-level CPN was modeled with clustered generalized estimating equations (GEE) and patient-level all-lesion CPN with multivariable logistic regression with propensity-score weighting. Temporal trends in utilization were measured with Cochran-Armitage tests, and temporal trends in CPN rates were estimated with GEE. RESULTS: Two hundred and forty-six patients were included; 421 lesions in 242 patients were analyzed for pathologic response. All-lesion CPN was associated with lower 5-year cumulative incidence of recurrence (0% vs. 7.1%), though overall survival did not differ (p = 0.066). Transarterial radioembolization (TARE) was associated with higher odds of all-lesion CPN than transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) alone (adjusted OR 4.83; p < 0.001), consistent at the lesion level (OR 4.59) and after propensity weighting (OR 4.54). Among lesions > 3 cm, CPN was 70.7% after TACE + ablation or TARE versus 44.1% after TACE alone (OR 3.26; p = 0.042). TARE use increased over the study period, and the rate of CPN in TARE-treated lesions increased by 4.8 percentage points per year (p = 0.006), whereas CPN after TACE did not change significantly (1.2 percentage points per year, p = 0.17). CONCLUSION: All-lesion CPN was associated with lower post-transplant recurrence. The probability of achieving CPN after TARE increased over 16.5 years while CPN after TACE remained stable. CPN represents an important therapeutic objective of pretransplant locoregional therapy and a pathological marker associated with favorable post-transplant outcomes. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE 2B: Retrospective Cohort Study.

articles.title: Multichannel Deep Learning Radiomics for Predicting Chemoimmunotherapy Response in Gastric Cancer: Multicenter Validation and Chemotherapy-alone Specificity Assessment.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a computed tomography-based model integrating multichannel deep learning and radiomics for predicting pathologic significant response (PSR) to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC), and to assess whether the model specifically captures immunotherapy-related phenotypes by testing it on a chemotherapy-alone cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter study included 455 patients with LAGC: 411 receiving NACI (split into training, internal validation, and external test set 1) and 44 receiving chemotherapy alone (test set 2). From three-dimensional (3D) segmentations, the largest axial, coronal, and sagittal slices were stacked as three-channel input for a pretrained ResNet50 to extract deep features; radiomic features were extracted from the 3D volume. Features were fused, reduced by the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and modeled with a support vector machine to construct a deep learning radiomics (DLR) signature. A combined model further incorporated mismatch repair status, programmed death-ligand 1 combined positive score, and tumor grade. Model performance was evaluated by area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis, with SHAP for interpretability. RESULTS: The multichannel model outperformed single-plane models (AUCs: 0.783, 0.749, 0.706). The DLR model achieved the highest AUCs (0.827, 0.802, 0.776), surpassing radiomics-only (0.756, 0.712, 0.691) and multichannel deep models. Critically, its AUC dropped to 0.597 in the chemotherapy-alone cohort. SHAP provided global and individual feature attributions. CONCLUSION: The multichannel DLR model accurately predicts PSR to NACI in LAGC. The substantial performance decline in the chemotherapy-alone cohort suggests that the captured imaging phenotypes may be more closely associated with immunotherapy-related response, rather than with general chemosensitivity, potentially offering a noninvasive, interpretable tool for pretreatment stratification.

articles.title: From Variability to Synchrony: Non-linear Development of Auditory Neural Responses During the First Year of Life.
articles.abstract: In humans, the first year of life is characterized by rapid developmental changes, including substantial brain maturation. As a result, neural responses to auditory stimuli undergo marked changes during this period. In this study, we followed 69 infants across their first year of life and recorded high-density electroencephalography (hdEEG) at 2 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum. Infants were presented with pure beep tones to examine the development of neural responses to auditory stimulation. We analyzed event-related potentials (ERPs), inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC), and event-related spectral perturbation (ERSP) responses to the beep tones and controlled for arousal state during stimulus presentation. We found that with increasing age, neural responses became more pronounced and showed reduced trial-to-trial variability. Phase synchronization increased from 2 weeks to later developmental stages in a broad low-frequency range (0.5 Hz to 13.6 Hz), indicating improved temporal alignment of brain responses over time. However, phase synchronization decreased from 6 to 12 months, suggesting a developmental transition towards more differentiated brain activity. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that auditory maturation during the first year of life follows a non-linear trajectory driven by dynamic changes in neural synchronization, reflecting the progressive refinement of functional neural circuits. Our results thus provide a critical benchmark for understanding the neural dynamics underlying sensory development during this period.

articles.title: Low-dose CT of the sacroiliac joints in suspected axial spondyloarthritis: Agreement with the rheumatologist's clinical diagnosis at baseline and two-year follow-up.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess agreement between baseline low-dose CT (ldCT) findings of the sacroiliac joints (SIJs) and the treating rheumatologist's clinical diagnosis, at baseline and after at least two years of follow-up, in patients clinically suspected of axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective observational study, adults suspected of sacroiliitis underwent ldCT of the SIJs between June 2023 and February 2024 at baseline. Two musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated examinations while blinded to clinical data. The rheumatologist's diagnosis at baseline and after at least two years, made with access to ldCT findings, served as comparator; no independent reference standard was available. Agreement with the clinical diagnosis, interobserver agreement and radiation dose were assessed. RESULTS: Seventy-nine patients (53 women, 26 men; mean age 43 years) were included; 25 (32 %) had a clinical axSpA diagnosis at 2 year follow-up. Both comparisons were subject to incorporation bias. Against the baseline clinical diagnosis, ldCT sensitivity was 81 % (95 % CI 57-93) and specificity 83 % (71-90); against the 2-year diagnosis, sensitivity was 80 % (61-91) and specificity 93 % (82-97), with positive and negative predictive values of 83 % and 91 %. Of 11 patients reclassified as axSpA during follow-up, 9 had a positive baseline ldCT. Interobserver agreement was substantial (kappa 0.68). Mean effective dose was 0.45 mSv. CONCLUSION: ldCT of the SIJs was feasible at radiation doses comparable to conventional radiography and structural lesions were interpreted reproducibly. Agreement with the rheumatologist's diagnosis is likely inflated by incorporation bias. Independent validation is required before changing imaging pathways.

articles.title: Exploring radiological criteria for extranodal extension in <15-mm cervical lymph nodes in oral cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify CT, MRI, and US features associated with pathological extranodal extension (pENE) and with nodal metastasis in cervical lymph nodes <15 mm in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 104 histopathologically evaluated nodes <15 mm from 42 patients: 32 pENE(+), 35 pENE(-), and 37 non-metastatic nodes selected for an unequivocally benign appearance. Shape, heterogeneity, necrosis, ill-defined borders, perinodal infiltration, and MRI-specific ENE signs (vanishing border, flare sign, shaggy margin) were evaluated on CT, T1w-MRI, T2w-MRI, CE-MRI, and US. In the primary comparison (pENE(+) vs. pENE(-) metastatic nodes), associations were analyzed with Firth logistic regression and false discovery rate correction, with and without size adjustment and with patient-level cluster-robust standard errors. The secondary comparison (pENE(-) metastatic vs. non-metastatic nodes) was descriptive. RESULTS: Perinodal infiltration and ill-defined borders on all modalities, and the MRI-specific signs, were associated with pENE (all q < 0.001), also after size adjustment and in the cluster-robust analysis. Necrosis was not significantly associated with pENE. Heterogeneity was frequent in pENE(-) metastatic nodes (91.4-96.3 %, except on T1w-MRI) but absent in the controls; because all controls were smaller than the metastatic nodes, this difference may partly reflect size. CONCLUSION: Perinodal infiltration, ill-defined borders, and MRI-specific ENE signs are potentially useful imaging signs of pENE in small nodes. Because the controls were selected for a benign appearance (spectrum bias), the secondary comparison does not reflect diagnostic performance in routine practice; all findings require confirmation in larger, consecutive cohorts that include equivocal nodes.

articles.title: Molecular adequacy of image-guided biopsy techniques in non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), image-guided biopsy must provide tissue for both diagnosis and biomarker-driven treatment selection. We systematically evaluated molecular adequacy of image-guided biopsy techniques for NSCLC biomarker profiling. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and CDSR were searched from inception to 30 May 2026, supplemented by reference screening and forward citation tracking. Eligible studies reported extractable numerator-denominator data for molecular/genotyping adequacy, NGS/genotyping adequacy, PD-L1 adequacy, diagnostic yield, or procedure-related complications. Random-effects meta-analyses of logit-transformed proportions used restricted maximum-likelihood estimation, with I2, τ2, and 95% prediction intervals. RESULTS: Twenty-six studies were included; 25 contributed to the main quantitative evidence base. The primary analysis included 23 study arms and yielded pooled molecular/genotyping adequacy of 89.5% (95% CI, 84.3-93.2%; I2 = 91.2%; τ2 = 1.070), with a 95% prediction interval of 48.4-98.7%. Pooled NGS/genotyping adequacy was 88.4% (95% CI, 80.9-93.1%; I2 = 91.6%), PD-L1 adequacy 93.9% (95% CI, 91.5-95.6%; I2 = 62.9%), and diagnostic yield 91.7% (95% CI, 86.3-95.1%). Sensitivity analyses did not materially alter the primary estimate. CONCLUSIONS: Image-guided biopsy provides high average molecular and biomarker adequacy in NSCLC, but performance varies substantially across clinical, procedural, and laboratory settings. Pooled estimates should be interpreted within study-specific testing denominators and workflows rather than as unconditional probabilities of successful biomarker profiling. Diagnostic success and molecular readiness should be reported as distinct outcomes.

articles.title: Exploring clinical variables and interventions to optimize utilization of multiphase CT for gastrointestinal bleeding: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Utilization of multiphase CT for gastrointestinal bleeding (CT-GIB) has experienced widespread growth in recent years, yet meaningful clinical outcomes associated with increased utilization remain uncertain. This study examines the overall positivity rate for CT-GIB, evaluates variables associated with a positive scan, and assesses the relationship between a positive CT-GIB and subsequent clinical interventions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: IRB approved retrospective analysis of 1,040 consecutive patients undergoing CT-GIB (Jan. 2019-Mar. 2025). Demographic (age, gender), hemodynamic (heart rate, blood pressure, shock index), laboratory (hemoglobin, platelets, INR, PT/P TT, albumin, BUN, creatinine) and clinical (anticoagulant use, hypertension, malignancy, cirrhosis) parameters were extracted from the electronic medical record within the 48-h periprocedural window. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify variables independently associated with three outcomes: a positive multiphase CT-GIB scan, endovascular intervention within 48 h, and endoscopic intervention within 48 h. RESULTS: Imaging volume increased 1,044% over the 6.25-year period. Active bleeding was detected in 143/1,040 (13.8%) of CT-GIB. Fourteen patients died within 48 h and were excluded from intervention analysis. Of the remaining positive cohort, 31/141 (22.0%), reflecting the cohort of 141 patients who survived the initial 48-h periprocedural window (i.e., after exclusion of 2 CTGIB+ patients who died within 48 h), underwent acute interventions within 48 h. Angiography was performed alone in 21/141 (14.9%), endoscopic intervention alone in 8/141 (5.7%), and both interventions were performed in 2/141 (1.4%). Variables independently associated with a positive multiphase CT-GIB: age > 65 years (OR = 2.15, 95% CI 1.41-3.30), male sex (OR = 1.54, 95% CI 1.06-2.22), and a nadir systolic BP < 105 mmHg (OR = 3.12, 95% CI 1.47-6.63). A positive multiphase CT-GIB was strongly associated with endovascular intervention (OR = 42.83, 95% CI 14.56-126.01; p < 0.001), but not with endoscopic intervention (OR = 1.53, 95% CI 0.73-3.23; p = 0.261). CONCLUSION: Multiphase CT-GIB volumes increased exponentially while positive yields remained low. This study demonstrates associations between CT-GIB findings and subsequent treatment pathways and lays the foundation for prospective studies aimed at determining whether interventional pathway-specific imaging selection can be applied without compromising clinical safety.

articles.title: Noninvasive imaging biomarkers of chronic liver disease severity and prognosis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers are associated with clinical severity and prognosis in chronic liver disease (CLD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 165 adults with chronic liver disease (CLD) who underwent gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI were included. Functional Liver Imaging Score (FLIS) was assessed on 20-min hepatobiliary-phase images, and Liver Surface Nodularity (LSN) was measured on contrast-enhanced axial T1-weighted images using semi-automated software. Spearman correlation analysis was performed for associations with Model for End-Stage Liver Disease 3.0 (MELD 3.0), and Albumin-Bilirubin score (ALBI). Time-to-event analyses for liver transplantation or death within 4 years were performed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the performance of FLIS for predicting 1-year transplant-free survival (TFS). RESULTS: FLIS showed moderate inverse correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = - 0.532, p < 0.001) and ALBI score (ρ = - 0.541, p < 0.001). LSN showed weak positive correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = 0.154, p = 0.049) and ALBI score (ρ = 0.184, p = 0.018). In univariable Cox analysis, older age, lower FLIS, higher MELD 3.0, higher ALBI score, and LSN cutoff ≥ 3 were associated with a higher risk of liver transplantation/death. In multivariable analysis, age (hazard ratio (HR), 1.05; p < 0.001), MELD 3.0 (HR, 1.08; p = 0.003) and FLIS group (0-3 vs 4-6 points; HR, 2.39; p = 0.007) remained independently associated with liver transplantation or death. For 1-year TFS, FLIS with an optimal cutoff of ≤ 3 yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.71 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.82). CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers, particularly FLIS, may provide noninvasive imaging markers of disease severity and prognosis in patients with CLD. Prospective studies with long-term clinical outcomes are needed to define their role in risk stratification and transplant decision-making.

articles.title: MRI criteria for adenomyosis: interobserver reproducibility of diagnostic features.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine which MRI features used in the diagnosis of adenomyosis are reproducible between readers, and whether a diagnostic certainty scale used in routine reporting can be applied consistently. METHODS: Prospective single-center study of 108 consecutive women referred for 3-T pelvic MRI after transvaginal ultrasound suspicion of adenomyosis. Three subspecialized radiologists, with 10, 8 and 5 years of experience, independently assessed all examinations, blinded to clinical data, ultrasound findings and to each other. Diagnostic certainty was recorded on a four-level ordinal scale (definite, probable, possible, absent). Agreement was quantified with Fleiss' kappa for the three readers, Cohen's kappa for pairs, and weighted kappa for ordinal variables. RESULTS: Agreement for the four-level scale was fair when unweighted (κ = 0.401) and substantial when quadratic-weighted (mean 0.663). No patient was rated probable by all three readers, and agreement across the definite-versus-probable boundary was null (κ = -0.013 to 0.143); collapsing the two categories raised it to κ = 0.581-0.698. For the two direct criteria it was substantial for myometrial hemorrhagic foci (κ = 0.650) and moderate for myometrial cysts (κ = 0.555). Among junctional zone measurements, agreement was moderate for thickness > 12 mm (κ = 0.530) but absent for junctional zone irregularity (κ = 0.048), which was non-evaluable in 21 of 108 examinations (19.4%). These examinations showed a higher prevalence of motion artifacts (p = 0.0005). Agreement on severity grade was moderate (κ = 0.441). CONCLUSION: Reproducibility varied widely across MRI features of adenomyosis, and the intermediate levels of the diagnostic certainty scale were not applied consistently. These findings argue for redefining the current MRI criteria for adenomyosis.

articles.title: IMPROving MYelin imaging in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (IMPROMYMS study): protocol for a prospective longitudinal study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: It is increasingly recognized that patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) may experience disability progression in the absence of clinical relapses and new lesions, a phenomenon known as progression independent of relapse- and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) activity (PIRMA). The biological basis of this type of progression remains poorly understood. Demyelination is the central pathological hallmark of RRMS. Conventional clinical MRI protocols focus primarily on detecting focal lesions. However, advanced imaging techniques that quantify myelin content can provide additional insights beyond visible lesions, helping to better understand the mechanisms that drive clinical deterioration. OBJECTIVE: Therefore, this study named IMPROving MYelin imaging in patients with relapsing-remitting Multiple Sclerosis (IMPROMYMS study) aims to apply myelin imaging techniques to study clinically defined disease progression in patients with RRMS, by assessing myelin content and comparing it to patients with RRMS without progression of the disease. METHODS: In total, 97 patients with RRMS will be included and followed for 2.5 years. Participants will undergo MRI scanning at baseline and after 2 years and have regular clinical follow-up visits. Besides conventional MRI, advanced imaging sequences will be scanned, including gradient spin echo (GRASE), multi-echo gradient echo (ME-GRE), diffusion and functional MRI. Additionally, blood samples will be collected longitudinally to assess circulating biomarkers of neuroaxonal damage and astrocytic activation. Participants can also use the smartphone symptom-monitoring app MS Sherpa to enable more frequent monitoring of functional changes in daily life. In addition, 30 healthy controls will be scanned once as a reference group. In this study, we expect to find radiological prognostic markers of an increased risk of developing PIRMA, so that disease management strategies can be altered accordingly.

articles.title: Flow diversion for posterior circulation aneurysms: a retrospective single-center 10-year experience.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Flow diverter stents (FDs) have expanded treatment options for posterior circulation aneurysms, but their use remains controversial due to a higher risk of ischemic complications. Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is mandatory after FDs implantation; however, clopidogrel shows variable effectiveness. Ticagrelor may represent an alternative, though data in posterior circulation flow diversion are limited. We report a single-center, 10-year experience using ticagrelor-based DAPT. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients treated with FDs for posterior circulation aneurysms between January 2014 and December 2024 under ticagrelor and aspirin. Previously ruptured aneurysms retreated with FDs following initial management were eligible. No aneurysm was treated during the acute phase of rupture. The primary endpoint was adequate occlusion (OKM C-D) at last imaging follow-up. RESULTS: Fifty-four patients were included, with 36 aneurysms (67%) treated as first-line therapy. Mean age was 56 ± 11 years. Aneurysms were most commonly located at the basilar tip (42%) with a median size of 6.5 mm (IQR 4-11). Imaging follow-up was available in 52 patients (96%) with a median duration of 34 months (IQR 19.0-49.5). Adequate occlusion (OKM C-D) was achieved in 63% at 6 months and 81% at last follow-up. Ischemic complications occurred in 17% of patients, including 11% symptomatic events, mainly in territories of jailed posterior cerebral arteries. One symptomatic event was fatal (2%). No hemorrhagic complications or delayed ruptures occurred. CONCLUSION: Flow diversion under ticagrelor-aspirin DAPT achieved adequate occlusion in 81%. Symptomatic ischemic complications occurred in 11% of patients, including one fatal event, predominantly following basilar tip aneurysm treatment. Four of the six symptomatic events occurred within ten days of planned ticagrelor discontinuation, raising questions about the optimal duration of antiplatelet therapy.

articles.title: Photon-counting computed tomography improves interobserver agreement in the evaluation of failed stapes surgery.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Failed stapes surgery presents a diagnostic challenge requiring high-resolution imaging to guide revision. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers improved spatial resolution and reduced noise compared with conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT). This study compared PCCT and EID-CT for identifying etiologies of failed primary stapes surgery, with emphasis on diagnostic accuracy, interobserver agreement, and interpreter confidence. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 38 patients with failed primary stapes surgery who underwent successful revision surgery and pre-revision CT were included; 18 underwent PCCT and 20 underwent EID-CT. Three expert reviewers independently determined the cause of surgical failure using intraoperative findings at revision as the reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy, interobserver agreement (Fleiss kappa), and reader confidence were compared between modalities. RESULTS: Overall interobserver agreement was higher with PCCT (κ = 0.75; 95% CI, 0.60-0.90) than EID-CT (κ = 0.44; 95% CI, 0.30-0.59), with non-overlapping confidence intervals for overall agreement and ossicular discontinuity. Consensus diagnostic accuracy did not significantly differ between modalities (88.9% PCCT vs. 85.0% EID-CT; p = 1.00), nor did interpreter confidence (4.33 vs. 4.17; p = 0.29). CONCLUSION: In this small cohort, PCCT demonstrated higher interobserver agreement than EID-CT without statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy or reader confidence, suggesting more reproducible assessment of failed stapes surgery.

articles.title: Support vector regression lesion-symptom mapping of post-stroke motor paresis: effects and evaluation of the minimum lesion threshold.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine how percentage-based minimum lesion thresholds (MLTs) influence support vector regression-based lesion-symptom mapping (SVR-LSM) of post-stroke motor impairment and to evaluate the maps using both spatial correspondence with the corticospinal tract (CST) and associations between map-based lesion load and motor impairment severity. METHODS: We retrospectively examined 131 patients with post-stroke hemiparesis. SVR-LSM was performed for upper-limb, hand, and lower-limb motor scores at admission and discharge using MLTs of 5-40% in 5% increments. Spatial correspondence between each group-level SVR-LSM map and a CST template was quantified using CST coverage, the map-in-CST proportion, and the Dice coefficient. For each patient, lesion load within each group-level SVR-LSM map was calculated and correlated with the corresponding motor score using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. RESULTS: Increasing the MLT progressively reduced the spatial extent of the SVR-LSM maps. The map-in-CST proportion increased, whereas CST coverage generally decreased, and Dice coefficients were generally highest at lower MLTs. Map-based lesion load was negatively correlated with the corresponding motor scores across all MLT conditions and all six domain-time-point combinations. The strongest correlations were observed at MLTs of 20-35% (absolute Spearman's ρ, 0.497-0.585). CONCLUSIONS: CST-based spatial correspondence and associations with motor impairment favored different ranges of MLTs. Lower MLTs produced broader maps with greater CST coverage, whereas moderate-to-high MLTs produced more restricted maps showing stronger associations with motor impairment severity. CST overlap alone should therefore not determine MLT selection, and the present findings do not support a single universally optimal MLT.

articles.title: The bloomy rind sign in leptomeningeal metastasis: a systematic review of neoplastic cases and a narrative review of non-neoplastic mimics.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The bloomy rind sign (BRS) - a non-enhancing, band-like or curvilinear T2/FLAIR hyperintensity along the brainstem surface - has been reported predominantly in leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) from lung adenocarcinoma, and more recently in non-neoplastic conditions. We performed a systematic review of neoplastic BRS and a narrative review of reported non-neoplastic mimics, in order to characterise the clinical and imaging spectrum of this finding and to propose a descriptive framework for differential diagnosis. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI and Wanfang from inception to 31 March 2026. No language filter was applied at the database-search stage, but eligibility was restricted to publications in English or Chinese. Because the search strategy was designed to ascertain neoplastic BRS, systematic-review methodology is applied only to neoplastic cases; non-neoplastic BRS-like reports identified during screening and citation tracking are summarised as a narrative review. Operational criteria developed for the present analysis were applied retrospectively to distinguish classic BRS from broader BRS-like brainstem-surface abnormality and from cases that could not be adjudicated. Individual patient data (IPD) - defined as patient-level data abstracted from published reports, not original datasets obtained from investigators - were extracted where available. Methodological quality was appraised with the JBI checklist matched to each study design. RESULTS: The systematic review identified 25 reports describing 50 patients with neoplastic BRS. Separately, five reports describing 12 patients with non-neoplastic BRS-like findings were summarised in the narrative review. A lung primary was confirmed or suspected in 49 of the 50 published neoplastic patients, the exception being one case of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia; adenocarcinoma was explicitly reported in 43 (86%), with one adenosquamous carcinoma, two cases described only as non-small-cell lung cancer, one probable adenocarcinoma without tissue confirmation and two lung carcinomas identified on imaging without a reported histological subtype. EGFR mutations were reported in 24 of the 28 patients with a documented molecular result (86%); no molecular result was reported for 21 of the 50, and testing was not applicable in 1. Gadolinium enhancement was absent or minimal in every case with documented post-contrast imaging. Restricted diffusion was present at the first reported BRS examination in 27 of the 28 patients evaluable at that time point (96%); the single baseline-negative patient developed restriction on follow-up, and restriction was also documented on repeat imaging in one further patient whose baseline diffusion status was unreported, so restriction was eventually recorded in all 29 patients in whom diffusion was reported at any time point. In the largest aggregate series it was reported in only 3 of 7 evaluable patients (43%), indicating substantial reporting bias. CSF cytology was positive in 12/18 (67%) patient-level cases with a documented conventional cytology result. Non-neoplastic BRS-like findings comprised autoimmune GFAP astrocytopathy (n = 9), varicella-zoster virus rhombencephalitis (n = 1), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (n = 1) and MOG-IgG-associated disease (n = 1). Treatment status before detection of the sign was reported in 18 of the 25 neoplastic reports: prior systemic or radiation therapy had been given in 12, most often an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, whereas in 6 the sign was documented before any oncological treatment; treatment status was not reported in the remaining 7. This limits separation of genotype from treatment-exposure effects. CONCLUSIONS: BRS has been reported predominantly in lung adenocarcinoma LM, particularly in EGFR-mutated disease, but these uncontrolled case-level data cannot establish diagnostic accuracy or specificity. Recognition of reported non-neoplastic mimics - GFAP astrocytopathy, VZV rhombencephalitis, NMOSD and MOGAD - is important when this pattern is encountered. We propose a descriptive diagnostic framework that requires prospective validation before clinical adoption.

articles.title: Initial Experience with the 6-10 mm TIPS Endoprosthesis: Technical Feasibility and Early Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the technical feasibility, hemodynamic effects, and early clinical outcomes of the 6-10 mm GORE VIATORR TIPS Endoprosthesis with Controlled Expansion, which extends the prior 8 mm deployment floor to 6 mm. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent de novo transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) creation with the 6-10 mm device between April and July 2026. Technical success was defined as portosystemic pressure gradient (PSPG) below 12 mmHg or ≥ 50% reduction from baseline. RESULT: Twelve patients (8 females, 4 males; mean age 57.1 ± 15.7 years; range 32-83 years) were included. Indications for TIPS creation were variceal hemorrhage (50.0%; n = 6/12), refractory ascites (33.3%; n = 4/12), and refractory hepatic hydrothorax (16.7%; n = 2/12). Final stent diameter was less than 8 mm in 91.7% (n = 11/12) of patients. Technical success was achieved in all patients, with mean PSPG decreasing from 16.7 ± 7.7 to 7.7 ± 2.9 mmHg (P <  .001) and no immediate adverse events. Shunt patency was 100% at short imaging follow-up (mean, 35.6 ± 25.0 days), with no reinterventions. No recurrent variceal hemorrhage occurred, and ascites improved or resolved in 77.8% (n = 7/9) of patients at short clinical follow-up (mean, 50.5 ± 23.3 days). Four of 11 patients (36.4%) experienced symptomatic HE after TIPS creation and one patient (9.1%) died during the follow-up period. CONCLUSION: TIPS creation using the 6-10 mm device is a technically feasible strategy with adequate short-term hemodynamic response.

articles.title: Recorded Use of Adrenal Ablation Relative to Adrenalectomy and Post-procedural Adrenal Insufficiency: A Real-world Network Analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Percutaneous adrenal ablation is a gland-sparing alternative to adrenalectomy for selected patients with benign functional adrenal disease. We compared recorded use, coded adrenal insufficiency within 30 days, and disease-control markers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a federated network of de-identified records (more than 150 million patients across 118 healthcare organizations), adults with adrenal diagnoses and ablation codes were compared with those with surgical-resection codes, excluding malignant and metastatic adrenal codes. We measured post-procedural adrenal insufficiency during days 1-30. Complication comparisons used one-to-one matching on 12 variables. Code capture was assessed in 10 confirmed procedures per group at one institution. RESULTS: Ablation codes identified fewer adults than surgical codes (364 vs. 11,568). After matching 300 pairs, adrenal insufficiency was recorded in 0% of ablation patients (0/298; exact 95% CI 0-1.23%) versus 14.5% of surgical patients (42/290; P <  .0001). Age and chronic kidney disease remained imbalanced. In a functional-disease comparison of ablation versus surgery, systolic blood pressure was 127 versus 131 mmHg (P =  .017), diastolic blood pressure was 73.9 versus 78.9 mmHg (P <  .0001), and serum potassium was 4.18 versus 4.22 mmol/L (P =  .40) (respectively). Local capture was 10/10 per group. CONCLUSION: In this observational comparison, ablation was associated with less coded post-procedural adrenal insufficiency within 30 days, yet ablation codes identified about one thirty-second as many patients as surgical codes. Uncertain network-wide procedure capture and residual confounding prevent conclusions about underuse or comparative safety. These hypothesis-generating findings support developing formal selection criteria and prospective studies. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3 retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: Liver T1, T2, T2*, and PDFF Mapping at 0.55 T Using Rosette MRF With Optimized Sequence Design and Deep Image Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Quantitative imaging on mid-field (0.55 T) MRI systems can suffer from poor precision due to low SNR. This work presents an MRF pulse sequence optimized with Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) and combined with a multi-echo deep image prior (DIP) reconstruction for co-registered T1/T2/T2*/PDFF mapping in the liver at 0.55 T within a single breath-hold. METHODS: A 20 s 2D multi-echo rosette MRF breath-hold acquisition was implemented on a 0.55 T wide-bore system. The sequence design was optimized via pseudorandom search using a CRLB-based objective for T1/T2 encoding and compared with reference designs. Data were reconstructed using (i) an iterative low-rank (LR) reconstruction and (ii) a multi-echo DIP jointly modeling TR- and echo-domain dynamics including B0 effects. Water/fat separation preceded dictionary matching for T1/T2; curve fitting was used to calculate T2* and PDFF was derived from M0 with noise-bias correction. The method was evaluated in numerical simulations, NIST and fat-fraction phantom scans, and in vivo acquisitions in 10 healthy subjects. A linear mixed-effects model was used to evaluate the effects of sequence design and reconstruction method on mapping accuracy and precision. RESULTS: Optimized sequences achieved lower CRLB cost than reference designs and, in simulations, CRLB cost was correlated with T1/T2 ROI variability (R2 = 0.76 LR; R2 = 0.83 DIP). Phantom experiments showed agreement with reference values. In vivo, both sequence optimization and DIP reconstruction significantly reduced the standard deviation of all four parameters in liver ROIs. CONCLUSION: CRLB-guided acquisition and multi-echo DIP reconstruction enable accurate and precise liver MRF T1/T2/T2*/PDFF mapping at 0.55 T in a single breath-hold.

articles.title: Improving Submillimeter BOLD fMRI Sensitivity With Localized Receive-Coil Design at 7 T.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether a dense, small-element receive array optimized for visual cortex imaging improves temporal SNR and BOLD sensitivity relative to a whole-head coil at 7 T, and whether this depends on spatial resolution. Two custom-built 7 T coils (32 receive, 8 transmit channels), one whole-head and one visual-cortex-optimized, were compared at 0.8- and 2.0-mm resolution. METHODS: Image SNR, temporal SNR, and BOLD sensitivity (suprathreshold spatial extent) were compared between coils at each resolution, acquired as a partial-slab protocol over the occipital lobe. RESULTS: The visual cortex coil yielded 2.5- and 2.8-fold higher image SNR at 0.8- and 2.0-mm resolution, respectively. At 0.8-mm, this only translated into a 1.3-fold increase in temporal SNR, but produced a 4.8-fold greater spatial extent of suprathreshold activation. Although contrast-to-noise-ratio (CNR) was only 2.4-fold higher for the visual cortex coil, decomposing CNR across the suprathreshold t-value distribution showed a 5.5-fold greater weighted CNR contribution, consistent with the larger spatial extent. At 2.0-mm resolution, temporal SNR was 1.4-fold higher with the visual cortex coil, but CNR and activation extent were similar between coils. CONCLUSION: The visual cortex coil's sensitivity advantage was higher at sub-millimeter resolution, where higher image SNR translated into higher temporal SNR and a 4.8-fold greater BOLD detection sensitivity, consistent with a 5.5-fold greater weighted CNR contribution across the suprathreshold t-value distribution. At 2.0-mm resolution, the SNR advantage did not translate into a detection benefit. The visual coil offers a practical advantage for ultra-high-field fMRI targeting fine-scale functional organization in the human visual cortex.

articles.title: Combining Cartesian and Non-Cartesian Acceleration Techniques With SPARKLING for 1 mm Isotropic Whole-Brain MPRAGE in a Minute.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: T 1   -weighted MPRAGE remains a cornerstone of clinical anatomical imaging, yet its long acquisition times constrain routine use. Established acceleration techniques, namely Parallel Imaging (PI) and Compressed Sensing (CS), tend to introduce substantial noise and blurring when pushed to high acceleration factors. Although they rely on fundamentally different redundancies, combining them synergistically remains an open challenge. METHODS: The GoLF-SPARKLING framework was extended to jointly exploit two acceleration mechanisms: PI-based uniform undersampling in the central k-space region and variable-density CS at the periphery, with independent acceleration factors in each zone. To preserve smooth signal evolution throughout the inversion-recovery period and avoid modulation artifacts, the acquisition trajectory was reordered accordingly. The resulting method was evaluated prospectively in vivo at 1 mm isotropic resolution and benchmarked against Wave-CAIPI and Poisson-disk sampling as respective PI and CS baselines. RESULTS: The proposed hybrid approach produced sharper, less noisy, and more stable whole-brain images in approximately 1 min than either acceleration strategy alone. Purely PI-based reconstructions were degraded by high g-factor noise, while exclusively CS-based reconstructions exhibited pronounced blurring. Furthermore, this method yielded lower average volumetric errors in downstream automated brain segmentation than state-of-the-art acceleration techniques, demonstrating its clinical utility. CONCLUSION: By jointly leveraging PI and CS, GoLF-SPARKLING achieves high acceleration factors that enable sub-minute, high-quality anatomical MRI. This translates into greater clinical throughput and more reliable imaging in patients who are challenging to scan.

articles.title: Reduced Hippocampal Subfield Volumes in Neonates with Low 1-Minute Apgar Scores Correlate with Umbilical Artery Blood Gas Parameters.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Perinatal asphyxia may induce brain injury, while the effects of transient hypoxia on hippocampal subregions remain unclear. Using the 1-minute Apgar score, this study examined its effects on hippocampal volumes and correlations with umbilical artery blood gas parameters (UABG), providing imaging evidence to evaluate hypoxia-related brain injury. METHODS: Neonates were assigned to the low Apgar score (LAS) group and the normal Apgar score (NAS) group. All subjects underwent 3D T1-weighted brain MRI for hippocampal volumetry. UABG indices, including pH, lactate (LAC), and base excess (BE), were collected. We performed an analysis of covariance with sex, postmenstrual age at MRI, and total brain volume as covariates, followed by correlation analysis. RESULTS: Multiple hippocampal subfields exhibited significantly smaller volumes in the LAS group (all FDR-corrected q < 0.05). Within-group analyses identified correlations between hippocampal volumes and UABG parameters. In the LAS group, left parasubiculum volume was correlated with pH and base excess, and in the NAS group, left parasubiculum volume correlated with the two indicators, while right tail volume correlated with pH. CONCLUSION: Neonates with lower 1-minute Apgar scores exhibit reduced volume of specific hippocampal subregions, correlating with umbilical artery blood gas parameters. These findings link transiently low 1-minute Apgar scores with hippocampal subregional morphology during the neonatal period. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: We investigated neonates with low 1-minute Apgar scores that normalized at 5 minutes and found their hippocampal subregional structural changes correlated with umbilical artery blood gas parameters.

articles.title: Clinical value of 18F-FDG PET/CT for detecting residual metastatic lymph nodes of DTC before initial radioiodine therapy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the adjunctive value of 18F-FDG PET/CT for assessing residual metastatic lymph nodes (MLN) before initial radioiodine therapy in postoperative DTC patients with high clinical suspicion of residual nodal disease. METHODS: This retrospective study included 835 postoperative patients with DTC who underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT before initial 131I therapy because of elevated stimulated thyroglobulin (sTg) and/or suspicious conventional neck imaging. MLN status was determined using a composite reference standard. Patient-level logistic regression was used to evaluate associated factors, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess discrimination and determine optimal cutoffs. A sensitivity analysis reassessed diagnostic performance using a reference assessment that excluded PET/CT information. RESULTS: Of the 835 patients, 452 (54.1%) were classified as having residual MLN. Under the composite reference standard, PET/CT showed a sensitivity of 84.5% and a specificity of 73.4%. After PET/CT information was excluded from the reference assessment, 104 patients were classified as indeterminate; among the remaining 731 patients, sensitivity remained similar at 85.9%, whereas specificity decreased to 40.1%. PET/CT contributed to N-stage revision in 149/835 (17.8%) patients, including a joint contribution with conventional imaging in 129 patients and an independent incremental contribution in 20 patients. Among patients with residual MLN, 275/452 (60.8%) exhibited an FDG-avid/131I-nonavid pattern. In TgAb-negative patients, multivariable analysis showed that nodal maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and sTg were independently associated with residual MLN (both P < 0.001). The corresponding ROC-derived cutoffs were 4.6 and 14.58 µg/L, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In postoperative DTC patients with a high clinical suspicion of residual nodal disease, 18F-FDG PET/CT may complement conventional imaging and biochemical assessment in identifying residual MLN and refining N-stage assessment.

articles.title: Spatial coupling between anosmia-related cortical alterations and regional gene expression: an imaging transcriptomics study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The impact of anosmia on brain cortical structure and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated causal associations between anosmia and cortical alterations using a multi-modal approach combining neuroimaging and genetics. METHODS: High-resolution structural magnetic resonance imaging was acquired from 52 patients with anosmia and 50 healthy controls to extract cortical surface area (SA) and cortical thickness (TH). Mendelian randomization (MR) was employed to assess the causal effect of anosmia on cortical structure using summary statistics from the ENIGMA consortium. Furthermore, integrating gene expression data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA), partial least squares regression (PLSR) and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) were used to identify genes associated with changes in SA and TH due to anosmia. Gene enrichment analysis and cell type-specific analysis were then performed to explore the potential molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Patients exhibited significantly reduced SA in the left rostral anterior cingulate and superior temporal sulcus, while TH was increased in regions including the left cuneus and supramarginal gyrus. MR analysis identified 11 cortical structural features nominally associated with anosmia, although none survived multiple comparison correction across 138 tests. Transcriptomic analysis identified genes correlated with these structural alterations, which were significantly enriched in synaptic pathways (e.g., postsynaptic membrane modulation) and specifically implicated GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons. CONCLUSION: Anosmia is causally associated with distinct cortical structural alterations. These regional changes are spatially coupled with molecular signatures involving synaptic function and neuronal plasticity, providing novel insights into the potential pathophysiology of olfactory loss.

articles.title: Bioabsorbable spacer-assisted high-dose proton beam therapy for unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer of the body or tail: a feasibility and safety study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Anatomical proximity to gastrointestinal (GI) organs can preclude dose-escalated irradiation for locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC). We evaluated the safety and feasibility of bioabsorbable spacer-assisted high-dose proton beam therapy (PBT) for unresectable LAPC of the pancreatic body or tail. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This exploratory retrospective analysis used retrospectively reviewed perioperative data and retrospectively or prospectively collected PBT data. Fourteen patients with presumed nonmetastatic LAPC underwent placement of a bioabsorbable polyglycolic acid (PGA) spacer. Thirteen received definitive PBT at 67.5 or 75 Gy (relative biological effectiveness [RBE]) in 25 fractions. The composite primary safety endpoint was the occurrence of a Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III surgical complication or a CTCAE grade ≥3 adverse event related to definitive PBT or concurrent chemotherapy. RESULTS: Spacer placement achieved ≥10 mm tumor-GI separation in all 14 patients; 13 completed definitive PBT. No Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III surgical complication occurred. Four of 13 definitive-PBT patients (30.8%) experienced at least one qualifying safety event: one experienced grade 3 nausea and three other patients experienced grade 3 leukopenia/neutropenia. No grade ≥3 structural GI injury was observed. Median follow-up was 19.3 months. Median overall and progression-free survival were 24.8 and 11.8 months, respectively; 1- and 2-year local control rates were 81.5% and 38.2%.
